title: Elections & political parties
examples: How do political parties help people choose leaders?
What is the main job of a political party before an election?
Can you explain what a political campaign actually involves?

explain.say: Political parties help people make choices in elections. They group people with similar ideas together.
One main role is to create and promote policies. Policies are plans for how to run the country.

items: Policies are plans for the country.
They suggest laws for different areas.
Parties use these to guide voters.

explain.say: Parties also help organize voters and candidates. They provide the structure for elections to happen.
During campaigns, parties try to share their message widely. They tell people why their policies are best.
In everyday life, a local council election is an example. Parties campaign on local issues like park funding.
A common mistake is thinking parties only talk about one thing. They usually cover many different areas of life.

draw.text: Mistake: Focusing on only one issue.

faq.q: What is the main difference between a political party and a single candidate?
faq.a: A political party is an organized group with many members and policies. A candidate is just one person running for office.
asks: Are parties just groups of people?
What is the difference between a party and a person?

faq.q: Do parties have to agree on everything to exist?
faq.a: No, parties exist because they bring together people who share a general set of beliefs. These beliefs can change over time.

faq.q: What is the goal of a political campaign?
faq.a: The main goal is to convince enough voters to choose their party or candidate. They do this by presenting their best policies.
asks: What are campaigns trying to achieve?

faq.a: Campaigns are meant to be fair, but sometimes there are disagreements about how much information is shared. Rules exist to keep them orderly.

faq.q: Do parties only exist in large countries?
faq.a: No, smaller communities and local areas can also have political groups. The size of the country does not determine the need for parties.
asks: Are parties only for big governments?

facts: Political parties bring together people with similar political views.
Policies are detailed plans for how the government should operate.
Campaigning involves trying to persuade voters to support a cause.
Parties help structure the process of electing representatives.

quiz.say: If a party focuses only on tax cuts, what are they neglecting?

options.show: Only talking about the next election.
options.say: Only talking about the next election.

quiz.why: A party must present a full plan, not just one part of it.

wrong.0: This is wrong because policies need to be for the long term.
wrong.2: This is tempting because money is always a big topic.
wrong.3: This is wrong because services like health are vital.

quiz.show: To group people with shared beliefs.

quiz.say: If a party uses leaflets and social media, what are they doing?
quiz.why: These are all methods used during a campaign to inform voters.

wrong.0: Leaflets only share ideas, they do not create law.
wrong.1: Campaigning does not give them power over dates.
wrong.2: They try to form one, but the vote decides that.
